ownSiteDefault: unreadable: the league's own site (premierliga.ru) answered every request on 2026-10-08 with a redirect to itself that asks for a browser check (the home page, the clubs page, the table page and the English site were tried), and that check was not worked around. Club sites were tried for three clubs: Zenit's squad page answers but prints no birth date on the list, Spartak Moscow's answers with a script check, and CSKA Moscow's squad address was not found. So no club's own site is one of its lists, and every club stands on independent publishers that print the birth date (critic's correction 15 of the Round 1052 brief).
method: Three squad lists were read for every club on 2026-10-08, each for the 2026-27 season with the season visible on the page or in the feed: Transfermarkt's 26/27 squad list in its detailed view, ESPN's roster feed for the 2026-2027 Russian Premier League, and FotMob's squad page (latest season 2026/2027). Transfermarkt's list is the spine: a man's shipped name is its spelling, his detailed position and his market value are its (the house convention of Round 1035). A man is a row only when Transfermarkt's list carries him AND at least one of the other two lists carries him too, matched by birth date with the shirt number or the spelling as a second witness, never by spelling alone. His birth date ships only where a second host prints the same date; his position group is the group at least two hosts put him in; his first nationality ships only where a second host names the same nation in Transfermarkt's spelling, and is null otherwise. His value is Transfermarkt's printed market value on that page, null where it prints none. Everybody else is in leftOut with the reason: on one list only; on two lists but not on Transfermarkt's (so there is no house spelling or value for him, and he is most often a man who has left); a birth date on one host; no group two hosts agree on; a name the game already holds somewhere else (decision 5 of the brief forbids moving him, so he is held out for the lead); a name the modern nationality map holds under another nationality; a second man of the same name inside the round. The lists were read once by scripts/research/gathered/fetch.mjs, which keeps each host's answer in a folder beside this file's working copy (three publishers' pages are not committed to a public repo), and scripts/research/gathered/build.mjs turns the kept answers into this file with no network, so the rows can be rebuilt and checked without asking the hosts again. Every man a host printed is either a row or in leftOut, with his id on that host in ids, and each list's size (listed) is counted a second way that does not go through the row parser; a squad row the parser cannot read stops the build. That rule is new on 2026-10-08: the first cut of the parser silently skipped every Transfermarkt row whose name carries an icon (captain, injured, suspended, not eligible), 50 of 437 rows, and filed 47 of those men as not on that list; they are rows now where they pass the rules. Wikipedia was not read. A club is partial when fewer than 8 men pass or more than half of the passing men have no value.

facts.note: two publishers for the first two steps; Sports.ru alone goes on (goal difference, then goals scored). The rules row still takes the default order (goal difference, then goals scored): the engine has no rule with a wins step, and its head to head rule would add a ledger of every league result to every save. The row's simplified text and the guide say what the game does.
